What We Do

Full-Service FQHC Revenue Cycle Management

FQHC billing operates under unique rules: encounter-based Medicaid payment, Medicare PPS rates, 330 grant compliance, and sliding scale fee schedules that run alongside insurance billing. PMEX manages every layer so your health center captures full FQHC encounter revenue on every patient.

Common FQHC Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Encounter not billed at FQHC rate because the visit type does not qualify as a billable encounter.

PMEX confirms qualifying encounter criteria before billing and ensures every eligible visit is billed at the FQHC encounter rate.

Medicare FQHC claim rejected because wrong type of service or bill type applied.

PMEX applies the correct Medicare FQHC bill type and type of service on every Medicare encounter claim.

Medicaid managed care wrap payment not reconciled, leaving supplemental revenue uncaptured.

PMEX tracks wrap payment eligibility per payer and reconciles wrap payments against encounter claims quarterly.

Sliding scale fee applied without confirming the patient income documentation on file.

PMEX confirms sliding scale income documentation is on file per UDS requirements before fee discounts are applied.

Behavioral health encounters not billed as qualifying FQHC encounters when they should be.

PMEX confirms behavioral health visit qualification for FQHC encounter rate billing per payer and state requirements.

Lab and ancillary services billed outside the encounter rate when they should be bundled.

PMEX determines which ancillary services are bundled in the FQHC encounter rate vs. separately billable per payer.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in FQHC Billing

FQHCs lose 14 to 24 percent of encounter revenue to visit qualification errors, wrong bill types, and wrap payment tracking failures.

PATTERN 01

FQHC Encounter Denied, Visit Does Not Qualify

Nurse-only visit billed as a qualifying FQHC encounter. Medicare requires the encounter include a face-to-face visit with an FQHC qualifying practitioner. Nurse-only visits do not qualify. Claim denied. Revenue lost with no rebilling option.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX confirms the visit type and rendering provider credential before billing every encounter as a qualifying FQHC encounter. Visits that do not meet the qualifying practitioner requirement are billed under the correct alternative code.

PATTERN 02

Medicare FQHC Claim Rejected, Wrong Bill Type

Medicare FQHC claim submitted with incorrect bill type. FQHC claims require bill type 77X. Claim rejected at the MAC before adjudication. Revenue delayed while correction and resubmission are completed.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies the correct FQHC bill type (77X) and type of service on every Medicare FQHC encounter claim before submission.

PATTERN 03

Medicaid Wrap Payment Not Captured

FQHC has a Medicaid managed care wrap agreement. Managed care organization pays the capitated rate. The supplemental wrap payment from the state is not tracked or reconciled. Wrap revenue, which can be 20 to 40 percent of total Medicaid FQHC revenue, is not collected.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks Medicaid managed care wrap payment eligibility per plan and per encounter, reconciling wrap payments against the state wrap payment report on a quarterly basis.

Questions

FQHC Billing Questions Answered

FQHCs are paid on a per-encounter basis for Medicare and Medicaid patients rather than per individual service. The all-inclusive encounter rate covers all services provided during a qualifying visit. We confirm encounter eligibility and bill the correct rate.

A qualifying FQHC encounter requires a face-to-face visit with a qualifying practitioner (physician, NP, PA, CNM, or qualified mental health provider). Nurse-only visits, lab-only visits, and administrative contacts do not qualify.

Under PPS, FQHCs receive a per-visit payment rate calculated from their historical costs and adjusted annually. We confirm PPS rate applicability and bill each qualifying Medicare visit at the correct PPS rate.

When Medicaid managed care organizations pay FQHCs at rates below the full FQHC encounter rate, the state is required to make a supplemental wrap payment for the difference. We track and reconcile wrap payments per state program.

We confirm income-based sliding scale discounts are applied in accordance with UDS reporting requirements, with income documentation on file per patient before fee reductions are applied.

Within 30 days, with encounter rate workflows, PPS compliance, and wrap payment tracking active from day one.
